== Lead trims ==

Regarding [https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Woolly_mammoth&oldid=prev&diff=1278776417 this edit].

Apologies for the misspelling of "woolly". Here's the rationale for the rest of the changes:
* {{tq|The origin of these remains was long debated and often explained as <s>being</s> the remains of [[legendary creature]]s.}} this is a simpler formulation that avoids the clunky "being" gerund.
* {{tq|The appearance and behaviour of '''this species'''...}} Why obscure the noun here? See [[WP:ELEVAR]]. This then allows to write the natural pronoun "it" instead of "woolly mammoth" in the following sentence.
* Paragraphs: we currently have three paragraphs in the lead, one of which is double the size of the others. You could call it a ''mammoth'' paragraph. Why not add a para break for readability?
[[User:Popcornfud|Popcornfud]] ([[User talk:Popcornfud|talk]]) 15:10, 4 March 2025 (UTC)

:::In character count, the second paragraph more than double the length of the first paragraph, and almost double the length of the third. [[User:Popcornfud|Popcornfud]] ([[User talk:Popcornfud|talk]]) 16:05, 6 March 2025 (UTC)

== Correct Information Of The Instruments ==
Along with the rest of the album, "Thriller" was recorded over eight weeks in 1982.<ref>{{cite magazine |url=https://ew.com/article/2008/02/07/quincy-jones-thriller/|title=Quincy Jones' 'Thriller' Memories|first=Simon|last=Vozick-Levinson|magazine=[[Entertainment Weekly]]|date=February 18, 2008|access-date=January 24, 2010}}</ref> It was recorded at [[Westlake Recording Studios]] on [[Santa Monica Boulevard]] in Los Angeles, California.<ref name="thrillertitleinterview3">{{cite web |first=Peter|last=Lyle|date=November 25, 2007|title=Michael Jackson's monster smash|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/culture/3669538/Michael-Jacksons-monster-smash.html|url-access=subscription|url-status=live|archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/20220112/https://www.telegraph.co.uk/culture/3669538/Michael-Jacksons-monster-smash.html|archive-date=January 12, 2022|access-date=January 24, 2010|work=[[The Daily Telegraph]]}}{{cbignore}}</ref> The engineer [[Bruce Swedien]] had Jackson record his vocals in different approaches, doubling takes and recording at different distances from the microphone. Some background vocals were recorded in the studio's shower stall.<ref name="thrillertitleinterview3" />

The bassline was performed on a [[Roland Jupiter-8]], not an [[ARP 2600]], from [[ARP Instruments]], as claimed by [[Anthony Marinelli]] in various interviews. In contrast: the "Falling Star", Wind and Theremin sounds were indeed created using an [[ARP 2600]], the “Marimba” Synth was performed on a [[Roland Jupiter-4]], the "Froggie" SFX was performed on a Casio keyboard, the Pipe Organ was performed on a [[Synclavier]], and the Bass Sweep/Synth Fall in the bridge was performed on a [[Minimoog Model D]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Mix Magazine – November 2008 |url=https://www.worldradiohistory.com/Archive-All-Audio/Mix-Magazine/00s/2008/Mix-2008-11.pdf |website=World Radio History |access-date=2025-03-28}}</ref> The verse pads were performed on a [[Roland Jupiter-8]] layered with a [[Prophet 5]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Carr |first=Dan |date=2022-11-30 |title=The synth sounds of Michael Jackson's Thriller (and how to recreate them in your DAW) |url=https://www.musicradar.com/news/thriller-synth-sounds |access-date=2023-03-19 |website=[[MusicRadar]] |language=en}}</ref> The percussion was created with a [[Linn LM-1|LM-1]] drum machine synced with a [[Roland TR-808|TR-808]] using a prototype [[Garfield Electronics Doctor Click]]. This was the first time multiple drum machines were synced together in recorded music.<ref>{{Cite web| title=Keyboards on 'Thriller' behind the scenes with eleven synthesists | url=https://gearspace.com/board/attachments/electronic-music-instruments-and-electronic-music-production/1136530d1732796884-thriller-bass-jupiter-8-not-arp-2600-a-img_1213.jpeg | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250423154312/https://gearspace.com/board/attachments/electronic-music-instruments-and-electronic-music-production/1136530d1732796884-thriller-bass-jupiter-8-not-arp-2600-a-img_1213.jpeg | archive-date=2025-04-23}}</ref> "Thriller" also features [[Rhodes piano]] performed by [[Greg Phillinganes]] and guitar performed by [[David Williams (guitarist)|David Williams]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Rogerson |first=Ben |date=2023-02-10 |title=Watch Greg Phillinganes recreate Michael Jackson's Thriller using the original synths |url=https://www.musicradar.com/news/thriller-synths-recreated-greg-phillinganes |access-date=2023-03-27 |website=[[MusicRadar]] |language=en}}</ref> Horns were arranged by [[Jerry Hey]] and performed by [[Jerry Hey]], [[Gary Grant (musician)|Gary Grant]], [[Larry Williams (jazz musician)|Larry Williams]], and [[Bill Reichenbach Jr.]].

To record the howls, Swedien set up tape recorders around his dog in a barn overnight, but it never howled. Instead, Jackson recorded the wolf howls himself, combined with [[sound library]] effects.<ref name="MusicRadar2">{{Cite news |title=The making of Michael Jackson's Thriller|url=https://www.musicradar.com/news/guitars/the-making-of-michael-jacksons-thriller-222109|access-date=2018-10-25|work=[[MusicRadar]]|language=EN-GB}}</ref> For the creaking doors, Swedien rented doors designed for sound effects from the [[Universal Studios Lot]] and recorded the hinges.<ref name="MusicRadar2" /> [[Vincent Price]] recorded his part in two takes; Jones, acknowledging that doing a voice-over for a song is difficult, praised Price and described his takes as "fabulous".<ref name="thrillertitleinterview22">{{cite web |last=Lyle|first=Peter|date=November 25, 2007|title=Michael Jackson's monster smash|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/culture/3669538/Michael-Jacksons-monster-smash.html|url-access=subscription|url-status=live|archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/20220112/https://www.telegraph.co.uk/culture/3669538/Michael-Jacksons-monster-smash.html|archive-date=January 12, 2022|access-date=January 24, 2010|work=[[The Daily Telegraph]]}}{{cbignore}}</ref>

:The main problem with this version is that the provided references don't support the claims.
:For example, the claim {{tq|The bassline was performed on a Roland Jupiter-8}} has no citation. I suspect (but it isn't clear) that you mean to support this claim with the [https://www.worldradiohistory.com/Archive-All-Audio/Mix-Magazine/00s/2008/Mix-2008-11.pdf Mix Magazine citation], but that makes no mention of "Jupiter" anywhere in the text. It does contain a blurry image of some kind of handwritten studio diagram, which includes "JP8" (meaning Jupiter 8), but we can't rely on our own interpretation of this diagram (that would be [[WP:OR|original research]]) and we have no way of knowing that it reflects the final song anyway. The [https://web.archive.org/web/20250423154312/https://gearspace.com/board/attachments/electronic-music-instruments-and-electronic-music-production/1136530d1732796884-thriller-bass-jupiter-8-not-arp-2600-a-img_1213.jpeg scan of the page from Keyboard mag you provide] mentions the Jupiter, but it doesn't say what it was used for. 
:I know on Gearspace there's a thread where enthusiasts are piecing together bits of evidence from various sources to try to establish what synths were used on what, but can't use the same process on Wikipedia to support claims. We have to rely on reporting what reliable published sources say directly, avoiding [[WP:SYNTH|synthesis]] and original research. [[User:Popcornfud|Popcornfud]] ([[User talk:Popcornfud|talk]]) 04:50, 9 November 2026 (UTC)

== Correct Information Of The Instruments ==
Along with the rest of the album, "Thriller" was recorded over eight weeks in 1982.<ref>{{cite magazine |url=https://ew.com/article/2008/02/07/quincy-jones-thriller/|title=Quincy Jones' 'Thriller' Memories|first=Simon|last=Vozick-Levinson|magazine=[[Entertainment Weekly]]|date=February 18, 2008|access-date=January 24, 2010}}</ref> It was recorded at [[Westlake Recording Studios]] on [[Santa Monica Boulevard]] in Los Angeles, California.<ref name="thrillertitleinterview3">{{cite web |first=Peter|last=Lyle|date=November 25, 2007|title=Michael Jackson's monster smash|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/culture/3669538/Michael-Jacksons-monster-smash.html|url-access=subscription|url-status=live|archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/20220112/https://www.telegraph.co.uk/culture/3669538/Michael-Jacksons-monster-smash.html|archive-date=January 12, 2022|access-date=January 24, 2010|work=[[The Daily Telegraph]]}}{{cbignore}}</ref> The engineer [[Bruce Swedien]] had Jackson record his vocals in different approaches, doubling takes and recording at different distances from the microphone. Some background vocals were recorded in the studio's shower stall.<ref name="thrillertitleinterview3" />

The bassline was performed on a [[Roland Jupiter-8]], not an [[ARP 2600]], from [[ARP Instruments]], as claimed by [[Anthony Marinelli]] in various interviews. In contrast: the "Falling Star", Wind and Theremin sounds were indeed created using an [[ARP 2600]], the “Marimba” Synth was performed on a [[Roland Jupiter-4]], the "Froggie" SFX was performed on a Casio keyboard, the Pipe Organ was performed on a [[Synclavier]], and the Bass Sweep/Synth Fall in the bridge was performed on a [[Minimoog Model D]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Mix Magazine – November 2008 |url=https://www.worldradiohistory.com/Archive-All-Audio/Mix-Magazine/00s/2008/Mix-2008-11.pdf |website=World Radio History |access-date=2025-03-28}}</ref> The verse pads were performed on a [[Roland Jupiter-8]] layered with a [[Prophet 5]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Carr |first=Dan |date=2022-11-30 |title=The synth sounds of Michael Jackson's Thriller (and how to recreate them in your DAW) |url=https://www.musicradar.com/news/thriller-synth-sounds |access-date=2023-03-19 |website=[[MusicRadar]] |language=en}}</ref> The percussion was created with a [[Linn LM-1|LM-1]] drum machine synced with a [[Roland TR-808|TR-808]] using a prototype [[Garfield Electronics Doctor Click]]. This was the first time multiple drum machines were synced together in recorded music.<ref>{{Cite web| title=Keyboards on 'Thriller' behind the scenes with eleven synthesists | url=https://gearspace.com/board/attachments/electronic-music-instruments-and-electronic-music-production/1136530d1732796884-thriller-bass-jupiter-8-not-arp-2600-a-img_1213.jpeg | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250423154312/https://gearspace.com/board/attachments/electronic-music-instruments-and-electronic-music-production/1136530d1732796884-thriller-bass-jupiter-8-not-arp-2600-a-img_1213.jpeg | archive-date=2025-04-23}}</ref> "Thriller" also features [[Rhodes piano]] performed by [[Greg Phillinganes]] and guitar performed by [[David Williams (guitarist)|David Williams]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Rogerson |first=Ben |date=2023-02-10 |title=Watch Greg Phillinganes recreate Michael Jackson's Thriller using the original synths |url=https://www.musicradar.com/news/thriller-synths-recreated-greg-phillinganes |access-date=2023-03-27 |website=[[MusicRadar]] |language=en}}</ref> Horns were arranged by [[Jerry Hey]] and performed by [[Jerry Hey]], [[Gary Grant (musician)|Gary Grant]], [[Larry Williams (jazz musician)|Larry Williams]], and [[Bill Reichenbach Jr.]].

To record the howls, Swedien set up tape recorders around his dog in a barn overnight, but it never howled. Instead, Jackson recorded the wolf howls himself, combined with [[sound library]] effects.<ref name="MusicRadar2">{{Cite news |title=The making of Michael Jackson's Thriller|url=https://www.musicradar.com/news/guitars/the-making-of-michael-jacksons-thriller-222109|access-date=2018-10-25|work=[[MusicRadar]]|language=EN-GB}}</ref> For the creaking doors, Swedien rented doors designed for sound effects from the [[Universal Studios Lot]] and recorded the hinges.<ref name="MusicRadar2" /> [[Vincent Price]] recorded his part in two takes; Jones, acknowledging that doing a voice-over for a song is difficult, praised Price and described his takes as "fabulous".<ref name="thrillertitleinterview22">{{cite web |last=Lyle|first=Peter|date=November 25, 2007|title=Michael Jackson's monster smash|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/culture/3669538/Michael-Jacksons-monster-smash.html|url-access=subscription|url-status=live|archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/20220112/https://www.telegraph.co.uk/culture/3669538/Michael-Jacksons-monster-smash.html|archive-date=January 12, 2022|access-date=January 24, 2010|work=[[The Daily Telegraph]]}}{{cbignore}}</ref>

:The main problem with this version is that the provided references don't support the claims.
:For example, the claim {{tq|The bassline was performed on a Roland Jupiter-8}} has no citation. I suspect (but it isn't clear) that you mean to support this claim with the [https://www.worldradiohistory.com/Archive-All-Audio/Mix-Magazine/00s/2008/Mix-2008-11.pdf Mix Magazine citation], but that makes no mention of "Jupiter" anywhere in the text. It does contain a blurry image of some kind of handwritten studio diagram, which includes "JP8" (meaning Jupiter 8), but we can't rely on our own interpretation of this diagram (that would be [[WP:OR|original research]]) and we have no way of knowing that it reflects the final song anyway. The [https://web.archive.org/web/20250423154312/https://gearspace.com/board/attachments/electronic-music-instruments-and-electronic-music-production/1136530d1732796884-thriller-bass-jupiter-8-not-arp-2600-a-img_1213.jpeg scan of the page from Keyboard mag you provide] mentions the Jupiter, but it doesn't say what it was used for. 
:I know on Gearspace there's a thread where enthusiasts are piecing together bits of evidence from various sources to try to establish what synths were used on what, but can't use the same process on Wikipedia to support claims. We have to rely on reporting what reliable published sources say directly, avoiding [[WP:SYNTH|synthesis]] and original research. [[User:Popcornfud|Popcornfud]] ([[User talk:Popcornfud|talk]]) 04:50, 9 November 2026 (UTC)

There's far too much focus on technical data and little of the article would be of interest (or make sense) to the general reader. The last paragraph in particular (beginning "Some devices operating MIDI 1.0 can "retrofit" some 2.0 features") is a perfect example of this. Per [[WP:AUDIENCE]] and [[MOS:JARGON]] this would need to be drastically trimmed back. [[User:Popcornfud|Popcornfud]] ([[User talk:Popcornfud|talk]]) 02:46, 5 October 2026 (UTC)

::I know it's frustrating to put a lot of work into an article and have it ripped out again. I also appreciate that you carefully researched these additions and cited them properly.
::The problem is, and I'm sorry to blunt, I think the prose was poor. It introduces ambiguity, adds needless elements and makes the whole page harder to digest.
::For example:
::* {{tq|Finnegan sought to recreate the harmonically rich distortion of a guitar amplifier being played at a high volume with the Centaur}}. This is a confusing sentence. It sounds like "a guitar amplifier being played at a high volume with the Centaur" is what Finnegan sought to recreate.
::* The addition of citations to the lead in violation of [[WP:CITELEAD]].
::OK, those things are easy enough to fix, and that's what I started off trying to do. But then I get to paragraphs like this (the first paragraph of the article body):
::* {{tq|With the Klon Centaur, Bill Finnegan of Boston, Massachusetts, sought to offer players "a more natural, transparent and amp-like overdrive" to be used in conjunction with an amplifier's own overdrive to add sustain and volume, as opposed to being used as the sole source of distortion with a clean amplifier.  Functionally a boost, the Centaur did however add to the signal a subtle midrange bump and distinctive distortion character.}} I think this paragraph will be unintelligible to the common reader. It isn't enough to merely quote what Finnegan says, we have to explain it plain English. What is a "natural, transparent and amp-like overdrive"? What does "functionally a boost" mean? What is a "subtle midrage bump and distinctive distortion character"? This reads like marketing copy for guitar equipment. Per [[WP:AUDIENCE]], Wikipedia articles must be written for a general audience. But this is how much of the prose now reads.
::As I wrote in my edit summary, my plan was to spend time to properly look at the information you added, which was all properly sourced, and find a way to integrate it that would hopefully satisfy both of us. I still think this is possible. [[User:Popcornfud|Popcornfud]] ([[User talk:Popcornfud|talk]]) 17:23, 20 December 2025 (UTC)

:::Say the reader has no prior knowledge of anything to do with Star Wars or the opinions of fans or critics or anything like that. They read the sentence "The film was critically acclaimed". 
:::Does this reader then think: "Ah! I notice Wikipedia specifies that it was acclaimed by ''critics'', but doesn't say anything about the reaction from Star Wars fans or the filmgoing public at large. This must be important."
:::No, of course they don't. They take the sentence in exactly the same way they would take the sentence "the film was acclaimed".
:::Now, if we think it's ''important'' for the reader to understand that the reaction from non-critics was different, then we should tell them that explicitly. In that case it's fair to write something like "positive reviews from critics but mixed reviews from fans" or whatever. But if we don't call that out, readers understand we're talking about critics. [[User:Popcornfud|Popcornfud]] ([[User talk:Popcornfud|talk]]) 09:44, 19 October 2026 (UTC)

:[Talk page stalker] I'm in two minds on this. Strictly grammatically what you're saying makes sense: the use of "his" here means he can only be referring to Sonic the character, not the franchise. But at the same time, I don't think anyone, including Miyamoto, would likely think that Sonic the character much resembles Mario, so I suspect something went wrong in translation.
:I can only speculate here, because the source only gives us the translation and not what Miyamoto originally said (he was almost certainly speaking Japanese and not English). But I think Miyamoto probably ''was'' talking about the franchise, not the character. This mixup could easily happen because Japanese often omits the grammatical subject from sentences. 
:So Miyamoto might have said something closer to, in very literally translated English, "Despite resemblance to Mario, there are some special points that make different", talking about Sonic the game. Then the translator misunderstood the grammatical subject and incorrectly went with "his" and "him" (instead of "its" and "it"). But I'm a pretty bad speaker of Japanese, so you should take this with a pinch of salt.
:In any case, we only have the translated English source to go on... which I think is self-contradictory and can be read either way. Shrug. [[User:Popcornfud|Popcornfud]] ([[User talk:Popcornfud|talk]]) 11:08, 3 September 2026 (UTC)

:::Because it provides a plausible explanation as to how this ambiguous quote might have come to be so ambiguous. FWIW, I just showed the quote to a native Japanese-speaking pal and he came to the same conclusion about what Miyamoto probably intended. But we can't know for sure. kind.description: They discuss music, video games, films, and music equipment, focusing on sources, article scope, and wording. They argue that claims need direct support from reliable secondary sources, not editors’ interpretations or promotional material. Citing Wikipedia’s rules, they support removing unsupported or excessive detail, simplifying technical language, and following sources for genres, series numbering, and descriptions of people.

examples.post_text: :::Presenting the info in prose is a great improvement, so thanks for that, but the lack of sources is a bigger problem. We shouldn't be adding any information to articles without first finding coverage of that information in reliable secondary sources. The most productive thing to do now would be to look at sources to find coverage for this stuff, add citations appropriately, and remove information that we can't find sources for. You can see a list of approved reliable sources at [[WP:RSINSTRUMENT]]. [[User:Popcornfud|Popcornfud]] ([[User talk:Popcornfud|talk]]) 14:35, 20 March 2025 (UTC)

examples.post_text:
*'''B, the shorter version'''. Some the citations in the longer version are dubious — Australian-Charts.com appears to be user-generated ([[Wikipedia:Reliable_sources/Noticeboard/Archive_320#Australian-Charts.com|RS noticeboard discussion here]]); Substack and SoundCloud are both [[WP:SPS]]; the YouTube video doesn't verify anything at all.

The description of the song as being "arranged for a big band lineup" is [[WP:OR]] and not mentioned in any of the sources. What's more, the abundance of sources creates an [[WP:CITEOVERKILL]] problem — simple claims should only require one or two sources. All in all, this is an [[WP:UNDUE]] amount of detail for a not very notable cover version. Let's keep it simple. [[User:Popcornfud|Popcornfud]] ([[User talk:Popcornfud|talk]]) 09:47, 3 July 2025 (UTC)

:There are two problems with this kind of thing:
:* We can only base such claims on what reliable secondary sources say. We can't formulate our own criteria for deciding what a "main" Metroid game is — that would be [[WP:OR|original research]]. If Nintendo themselves have a criteria (and I think they do, on some official website somewhere), great, but ideally we wouldn't use that as it's a [[WP:PRIMARY]] source.
:* Sentences like the proposed "Ex. Metroid _____ is the Xth main Metroid game, and the Xth game in the (2D Metroid/Metroid Prime) series" are complicated and fiddly and won't mean much to most readers. It gets into the weeds with explaining (or rather overexplaining) and quickly gets into diminishing returns.
:I agree that the inconsistency across the Metroid articles is a problem, but I don't know what the solution is right now. There was (or is) a similar problem with [[Resident Evil Requiem]]. [[User:Popcornfud|Popcornfud]] ([[User talk:Popcornfud|talk]]) 04:37, 15 October 2026 (UTC)

examples.post_text: :This article is a long way from GA quality. There are many unsourced statements, and statements cited to unusuable sources (such as personal/hobbyist websites and online stores such as Sweetwater). There's far too much focus on technical data and little of the article would be of interest (or make sense) to the general reader. The last paragraph in particular (beginning "Some devices operating MIDI 1.0 can "retrofit" some 2.0 features") is a perfect example of this. Per [[WP:AUDIENCE]] and [[MOS:JARGON]] this would need to be drastically trimmed back. [[User:Popcornfud|Popcornfud]] ([[User talk:Popcornfud|talk]]) 02:46, 5 October 2026 (UTC)

user_page.connections: The user page’s writing essays and Capote quotation about scissors align with edits trimming repetition and shortening prose, notably removing “the film” in The Truman Show, and talk-page arguments for simpler wording and less excessive detail.

article_edit_history.connections: On music, film and video-game articles, they tighten prose, reorganize material and correct sourcing, including release details and Brian Eno’s chronology. Their removal of repeated “the film” matches their user-page essays; discussions on article and user talk pages similarly emphasize concise wording, secondary sources and limiting detail.

article_talk_history.connections: On Creep and Ableton Live talk pages, they question sourcing; on Metroid and MIDI, they also discuss excessive technical detail. These discussions parallel their music and video-game editing, prose trimming, user-page essays on concise writing, and user-talk requests for secondary sources and limits on track-list additions.

user_talk_history.connections: Their user-talk discussions of entertainment sourcing, track lists, wording, and formatting parallel their music, game, and film edits and article-talk discussions about secondary sources and excessive detail. Advice on correcting typos also aligns with their user-page writing essays.

in_the_discussion.connections: Their demand for secondary sources supporting Hyde’s synthesizer and its importance matches their sourcing arguments on Ableton Live, MIDI, and user talk pages. Their discussion also overlaps with their other music-equipment talk-page activity and removal of unsupported details.

user_page.judgment: They seem to present themselves as an assertive advocate for concise, precise writing, sharing a focused collection of editing essays rather than personal details.

article_edit_history.judgment: Their edits seem predominantly constructive: useful copyediting across film and game articles, plus sourced additions and chronological improvements on Brian Eno and Radiohead topics. However, occasional grammatical mistakes, malformed citations and overaggressive trimming reduce clarity or remove useful context.

article_talk_history.judgment: They seem to prioritize reliable sourcing and concise, accessible prose in music, games, and film articles. Usually direct, civil, and policy-focused, they can be collegial and self-correcting but become sarcastic or dismissive in prolonged disputes, especially over Michael Jackson.

user_talk_history.judgment: They seem to focus on entertainment sourcing, track lists and prose, usually offering concise, guideline-based corrections. Generally civil and helpful, they acknowledge mistakes and alternatives, but become blunter and occasionally dismissive in disputes, particularly over Michael Jackson-related editing.

in_the_discussion.judgment: In this discussion, they seem firm, civil, and sourcing-focused, consistent with their usual direct manner and less dismissive than in their more contentious disputes.
